summary: Swain/Jackson line lookout on Cherokee reservation land, built 1932; still standing with a locked cab, climbable stairs, and a 1.2-mile round-trip hike.

facts.design: steel tower planned as six eight-foot sections (1932 newspaper); NHLR describes an 80-foot metal tower with a 7x7-foot metal cab; MyHikes gives 60 feet

access.note: MyHikes calls it one of two publicly accessible towers in the Qualla Boundary; the cab is locked but the stairs can be climbed; the entrance gate may be closed; the land is tribal and tribal visitor rules were not confirmed

visit.trail_note: 1.2-mile round trip from the gate on Barnett Fire Tower Road (BIA 406) beside the Blue Ridge Parkway; park at the gate

events.note: construction under way in August 1932 (foundation done, two of six steel sections set); NHLR and MyHikes both date the tower to 1932
March 1933: the regular warden, a Cherokee man named Crow, was ill and another man served in his place
National Historic Lookout Register registration date October 31, 2006

evidence.supports: tower sits in the Qualla Boundary of the Cherokee Indian Reservation, adjacent to the Smokies
evidence.quote: Located in the middle of the Qualla Boundary of the Cherokee Indian Reservation adjacent to the Great Smokey Mountains National Park

evidence.supports: built 1932; 80-foot metal tower with a 7x7-foot metal cab
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1932, the 80' metal tower with 7'x7' metal cab

evidence.supports: foundation finished and two of six eight-foot steel sections set in August 1932
evidence.quote: has completed the foundation and placed two of the steel sections. Six sections, eight feet each, are to be erected.

evidence.supports: the foundation and steel sections are from the article dated August 4, 1932
keeper's cabin still to be built; a Cherokee keeper expected but not yet appointed
evidence.quote: A cabin, to house the keeper of the lookout, is also to be built. A Cherokee Indian is to be placed in the lookout, but he has not been appointed as yet.

evidence.supports: article of March 1, 1933: regular warden Crow was ill and another man took his place
evidence.quote: The regular warden, Crow, a Cherokee Indian, who is in charge of the fire tower at Barnett's Knob is ill but another man is in his place until he recovers.

evidence.supports: the warden item is from the article dated March 1, 1933
60-foot steel tower built in 1932 (height conflict with NHLR's 80 feet)
evidence.quote: The 60-foot steel tower was originally built in 1932 on the highest point.

evidence.supports: register calls it the last active lookout on the Reservation
evidence.quote: Barnett Knob Lookout Tower is the last active lookout on the Reservation.

evidence.supports: registered with the NHLR on October 31, 2006
hiking guide says views of forest fires lasted until the early 2000s
evidence.quote: provided bird’s-eye views of forest fires until the early 2000s.

evidence.supports: administered by the Bureau of Indian Affairs
tower remains in very good condition because of ongoing use for communications
evidence.quote: remains in very good condition today due to its ongoing use for communications.

evidence.supports: antenna towers and trees make the views from the stairwell poor
evidence.quote: surrounding antenna towers and surprisingly tall trees obscure good views from the stairwell.

evidence.supports: cab is locked, but the stairs can be climbed for views above the treeline
evidence.quote: The cab is locked, but you can climb the stairs to get views above the treeline.
The Barnett Knob Lookout Tower is a 1.2-mile roundtrip hike to a 60-foot historic fire tower located off the Blue Ridge Parkway near Cherokee, NC.

evidence.supports: park at the gate on Barnett Fire Tower Road / BIA 406
evidence.quote: Park at the gate for the Barnett Fire Tower Road/BIA 406 beside the Blue Ridge Parkway.

evidence.supports: parkway often closed through this section in winter
evidence.quote: The Blue Ridge Parkway is often closed through this section during the winter, so make sure to check the real-time closures map before you visit.

evidence.supports: only the hiking guide describes public access
evidence.quote: The Barnett Knob lookout tower is one of two remaining publicly accessible towers in the Qualla Boundary

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives an 80-foot tower and MyHikes gives 60 feet (about 18 m). Height is left out of facts until a third source resolves the disagreement.
NHLR lists Swain County, while the 1932 newspaper places the tower on the line between Swain and Jackson counties. The record keeps Swain.
NHLR gives 4,771 ft (1,454 m) and MyHikes gives 4,665 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.

notes_for_editor: Height (80 ft NHLR vs 60 ft MyHikes) and elevation disagree between sources, so height is not published as a fact. The 1932 newspaper items describe construction in progress, so the completion year rests on NHLR and MyHikes. Access level comes from a hiking guide and the land is tribal; BIA and tribal visitor rules were not checked. The fire-watch end date is not firm. Staffing is not published as a fact: the 1933 warden watch is in the timeline, but the vocabulary has no value for it and no current staffing source was found. The 1934 CCC road and a 1934 marriage item in the same newspaper page were left out as not relevant.
